answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A terrace delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A grove check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A walnut penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 287 identities need 287 bonds of 68 tokens, 8668 dollars of hardware and 35 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
